acceptance: Red-first: a fresh cycle on a bound scope whose ancestor has no ledger reaches audit with a manifest (or a recorded release) and is not failed by the gate.
A deleted or rewritten manifest of an adopting cycle still blocks.
100% coverage on each changed function; zero code comments; the continuation and defect-ledger docs name the change.
fix: At claim time, when the registry binds the scope, either adopt the binding (write the continuation manifest into the new workspace before scout) or, when the ancestor has no ledger and its snapshot is superseded, release the binding through the existing transaction with a recorded reason. Keep the anti-tamper rule for a manifest that was deleted or rewritten. Give the gate's FAIL a failure class so the repair ladder can act.
routed_reason: built by a claude-cloud bridge seat in the operator credit window on 2026-11-04
source: console 2026-11-04 wave 152: resumed cycle 2109 (latency-gates-t6-wave-latency-check) passed audit 7/7 with red_count 0, yet the defect-ledger gate forced FAIL: 'this workspace holds no continuation manifest, but the root-owned continuation-registry.json binds this lane's scope to cycle-2092'. Cycle 2092 left no defect ledger, so the binding carries no inherited defect. 2107 (bound to 2090) and 2108 (bound to 2093) have the same shape.
summary: defectledger.arm blocks when the registry binds the scope but the workspace has no continuation manifest. A cycle that started fresh on a bound scope (without adopting the binding) therefore fails every audit, with no failure class, so it gets no repair round; good work fails for bookkeeping. The concurrent resume of 2026-11-03 made several such old cycles run again. The cycle writes its own manifest only at its end, after the audit.
title: A fresh cycle on a scope that the continuation registry binds must adopt the binding or release it; today it fails audit deterministically
